oet_note: HCPC accepts the OET for occupational therapists (a regulated/protected profession) from 29 January 2025. OET publishes an Occupational Therapy-specific version of the test. On HCPC's own certificate-of-English-language-proficiency page the requirement is expressed in the current numeric OET scoring: an overall score of at least 1400 with no individual sub-test (Listening, Reading, Writing, Speaking) below 300. In legacy OET grade terms, 300 corresponds to Grade C+ (minimum per sub-test) and the 1400 total equates to roughly an average of Grade B — hence secondary sources commonly describe HCPC's OET standard as "Grade B". Speech and language therapists face a higher bar (1800 total / 400 each), but occupational therapists fall in the "most professions" band (1400/300). Certificate must be no more than two years old at application.

oet_note: HCPC accepts the profession-specific OET (Occupational English Test) for radiographers as evidence of English language proficiency. OET was added to IELTS and TOEFL as a recognised provider from November 2024, with the requirement applying to applications from 29 January 2025. The finalised requirement on HCPC's official 'Certificate of English language proficiency' page is a minimum OET score of 1400 with no element (Listening, Reading, Writing, Speaking) below 300 — i.e. at least grade C+ in every sub-test. In OET grade terms this equates to roughly an overall grade B with a minimum of C+ in any paper (the equivalency HCPC benchmarked against its IELTS 7.0 / no element below 6.5 standard). Applicants whose relevant primary qualification was obtained/taught in a country on HCPC's English-predominant qualifying list (e.g. Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, USA) are exempt from any English test.

oet_note: HCPC added OET (Occupational English Test) as an approved English language test for international applicants effective 00:01 GMT, 29 January 2025. OET publishes a Dietetics-specific version and HCPC explicitly lists Dietitians among the limited professions for which OET is accepted. HCPC states the requirement in OET numeric scores rather than letter grades: for Dietitians, an overall score of 1400 with no element below 300. In OET's letter-grade scheme, 350–450 = Grade B and 300–340 = Grade C+, so this equates to effectively a Grade B overall average with a minimum of Grade C+ in each of the four sub-tests (Listening, Reading, Writing, Speaking). Note OET is NOT available for all HCPC-regulated professions — it is offered only for a limited set including Dietitians, Chiropodists/Podiatrists, Occupational therapists, Physiotherapists, Radiographers, and Speech and language therapists (SLTs require the higher 1800 / no element below 400). facts.value: Dietetic Skills Recognition (DSR) is a three-stage process assessing skills against the National Competency Standards: Stage 1 — DSR eligibility assessment (professional recognition in home country, recency of practice within 3 years, English proficiency, a 4-year tertiary degree covering human biosciences and food/nutrition science with >=100 days supervised placement); up to 6 weeks. Each exam may be attempted up to 3 times; all stages plus joining the APD Program must be completed within 3 years of DSR approval. Cultural Awareness (Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander) assessment required. Passing enables APD status, Medicare/DVA provider numbers, and private health insurer recognition.

oet_note: HCPC explicitly accepts the OET (Occupational English Test) for speech and language therapists, but at a HIGHER threshold than most other HCPC professions. General HCPC professions need OET 1400 total with no element below 300; speech and language therapists must achieve OET 1800 total with no element (Listening, Reading, Writing, Speaking) below 400. On the OET 0-500 numerical scale each subtest maps to a grade (A = 450-500, B = 350-440, C+ = 300-340). So the SLT requirement of no element below 400 is effectively at least a strong Grade B in every subtest, with a total of 1800 (average 450 ≈ Grade A). OET publishes a Speech Pathology version of the test; candidates would sit the profession-relevant version. Certificate must be no more than two years old at the point HCPC receives the application, and taken at an official test centre (not remotely).

facts.value: Two pathways to have overseas qualifications recognised: (A) Mutual Recognition Agreement (MRA) — for applicants holding FULL certification with a signatory association (ASHA (USA), SAC (Canada), RCSLT (UK), IASLT (Ireland), NZSTA (NZ)) AND who completed their education in an MRA signatory country. (B) Overseas Qualified Competency Assessment (OSQCA) — for those ineligible for MRA. OSQCA launched 1 February 2026 and has FOUR phases: Phase 1 Eligibility (ID + English + recent-practice evidence); Phase 2 Learning (online modules: ethics, evidence-based practice, cultural competency); Phase 3 Written Assessment (portfolio across communication and swallowing cases); Phase 4 Verbal Assessment (videoconference interview, only if Phase 3 passed). Up to three resubmissions per phase within a 2-year validity window. This is an assessment-of-competency pathway, not a single exam.

facts.value: Internationally qualified podiatrists have two main pathways: (1) Recognised international qualification pathway - if the Board has previously assessed the same qualification (same provider, year, degree title) as substantially equivalent, the applicant may apply directly for general registration; (2) Qualification assessment pathway - submit a portfolio (form PNAQ-70, 'Portfolio for the assessment of non-approved qualifications') for the Board to assess against approved qualifications (outcomes: substantially equivalent, relevant to practice, or ineligible), then apply. Assessment references National Law sections 52-53. New Zealand podiatrists with a current practising certificate may use the Trans-Tasman Mutual Recognition Act 1997. No universal single national bridging exam is mandated; outcome depends on portfolio assessment. English language standard must also be met.

facts.value: Non-recognised qualifications are verified through portfolio assessment (PNAQ-70) under National Law ss 52-53, checking substantial equivalence of the education provider, year and degree. Applicants must also satisfy AHPRA's standard registration checks (identity, qualifications, recency/criminal history) applicable to all National Boards. English proficiency evidenced via an accepted test or an education-based pathway under the English language skills registration standard.

facts.value: Registration is separate from immigration.
